title: Sauce boss

clues.t: My name may come from a fermented fish sauce in southern China.
Early English versions of me were made from mushrooms, walnuts or oysters.
My most famous brand slapped '57 varieties' on the label even though it made more than 60 products.
Tapping the '57' on my glass bottle's neck is meant to get me flowing.
Americans call me one thing; Aussies and Brits often call me 'tomato sauce'.
I'm the red stuff you squirt on chips and burgers.

pearl: Heinz started bottling it in 1876. Legend says 5 was Henry Heinz's lucky number and 7 his wife's.

title: Neck and neck

clues.t: My babies' first experience of life is a drop of about two metres.
My closest living relative is the stripy-legged okapi.
A group of us is called a 'tower'.
I have the same number of neck bones as you: seven. Mine are just huge.
My tongue is about 45 cm long and great for stripping acacia leaves.
I'm the tallest animal on Earth, with patches like a jigsaw.

pearl: No two giraffes have the same coat pattern. Nature's version of a fingerprint.

title: Torch song

clues.t: I was a working lighthouse for about 16 years.
I used to be shiny brown. Weather turned me green.
My iron skeleton was designed by the same man behind a famous tower in Paris.
Broken shackles lie at my feet, and my tablet reads JULY IV MDCCLXXVI.
I was shipped across the Atlantic in hundreds of pieces packed in crates.
A gift from France, I hold a torch over New York Harbour.

pearl: Her torch arm has been closed to visitors since 1916, after a nearby explosion damaged it. She's waved from a distance ever since.

title: Land of the rising fun

clues.t: A recount in 2023 found I have over 14,000 islands, double the old figure.
A rail company here formally apologised because a train left 20 seconds early.
Fried chicken from a certain colonel is a Christmas tradition here.
One of the world's oldest companies, a temple builder, was founded here in 578.
Farmers here grow square watermelons to fit in fridges.
Sushi, bullet trains, Mount Fuji, Tokyo.

pearl: The 20-second apology made global headlines. Punctuality is a national sport.

title: Stuck on you

clues.t: A Swiss engineer invented me after a walk with his dog in 1941.
Some NASA astronauts stuck me inside their helmets to scratch their noses.
My name mixes the French words for 'velvet' and 'hook'.
My own company made a music video begging people not to use my name for copies.
I'm two strips: one of tiny hooks, one of tiny loops.
Burrs inspired me. I go RRRRIP on kids' shoes.

pearl: The company would like you to say 'hook-and-loop'. Nobody does.

title: Unsinkable box office

clues.t: I'm longer than the real event: about 3 h 14 min vs about 2 h 40 min.
I was the first film ever to take $1 billion at the box office.
I tied the record for the most Oscars won: 11.
The famous portrait sketch was drawn by the director himself.
'I'm the king of the world!' was shouted from my bow.
A rich girl, a poor artist, a ship and an iceberg. Ends cold.

pearl: Fans have argued for decades that there was room on that door. Draw your own conclusions.

title: Lady Lindy

clues.t: I launched my own lines of clothing and luggage.
I once whisked the First Lady away from a White House dinner for a night flight.
In 1935 I was the first person to fly solo from Hawaii to California.
In 1932 I became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.
I vanished over the Pacific in 1937 trying to fly around the world.
America's most famous aviatrix. Search parties are still looking.

pearl: She was hunting for tiny Howland Island when contact was lost. The mystery still sells documentaries.

title: Crack the case

clues.t: In 2005, 110 people won big Powerball prizes thanks to me.
Despite my reputation, I'm rarely found in China.
My likely ancestor is a Japanese cracker.
I was popularised in California in the early 1900s.
I'm folded while still warm, with a strip of paper tucked inside.
Crack me open after your Chinese takeaway to learn your future.

pearl: The 110 winners all played the numbers printed on the same batch of fortunes. Lottery officials suspected fraud. It was just biscuits.

title: Black tie only

clues.t: I can drink seawater; a gland above my eyes filters out the salt.
Some ancient relatives of mine were about as tall as a person.
Some males propose with a carefully chosen pebble.
Emperor dads balance an egg on their feet for about two months without eating.
I'm a bird, but I only fly underwater.
Waddling, tuxedoed, and hanging around Antarctica.

pearl: Their tuxedo is camouflage: dark backs hide them from above, white bellies from below.

title: Rock concert

clues.t: In 1915 I was sold at auction for £6,600, reportedly as a present for a man's wife.
Some of my stones were dragged roughly 250 km from Wales.
In 2024 scientists found one of my biggest stones came from northern Scotland.
I line up with the sunrise on the summer solstice.
I'm around 5,000 years old and nobody's totally sure what I was for.
A ring of giant standing stones in Wiltshire, England.

pearl: The buyer, Cecil Chubb, gave it to the nation three years later. Best regift ever.

title: Sorry, eh?

clues.t: Santa's postcode here is H0H 0H0.
More than half of the world's lakes are mine.
I have the longest coastline on Earth.
Pineapple on pizza was invented here, by a Greek immigrant in Ontario.
I keep a strategic maple syrup reserve, and thieves once stole millions of dollars of it.
Mounties, moose, hockey and a maple leaf flag.

pearl: The great maple syrup heist of 2011-12 saw about C$18 million of syrup vanish. Sticky fingers.

title: Insert coin

clues.t: My earliest known ancestor dispensed holy water in a temple about 2,000 years ago.
Its inventor was the ancient Greek engineer Hero of Alexandria.
In 1880s London a version of me sold postcards.
Japan has millions of me, selling everything from hot soup to umbrellas.
I work around the clock and never ask for a tip.
Pop in a coin or tap your card, and out drops a snack.

pearl: Hero's machine used a coin dropping onto a lever to open a valve. Ancient engineering, modern snack.

title: Something fishy at the beach

clues.t: My star kept breaking down, so you barely see it for most of the film.
I was filmed on Martha's Vineyard, standing in for a fictional island town.
I'm often credited as the first summer blockbuster, in 1975.
'You're gonna need a bigger boat' was reportedly improvised.
Two low notes on my soundtrack still make swimmers get out of the water.
A great white shark terrorises the beachgoers of Amity Island.

pearl: The mechanical shark kept sinking in salt water. Leaving it out made the film scarier. Happy Friday the 13th.

title: Poetical science

clues.t: At 12 I planned a flying machine and wrote a guide called 'Flyology'.
My father was a scandalous poet I never got to know.
My mother had me tutored in maths to keep any poetic madness at bay.
A US military programming language is named after me.
In 1843 I published notes that included what many call the first computer program.
I worked with Charles Babbage on his Analytical Engine. Countess, coder, legend.

pearl: Her father was Lord Byron, who left when she was a baby. Ada Lovelace Day is the second Tuesday of October.

title: Not as French as it looks

clues.t: My ancestor is an Austrian bread roll called the kipferl.
A Viennese baker opened a shop in Paris in the 1830s and made me famous.
The tale that I was invented to celebrate beating the Ottomans is a myth.
In French bakeries, a straight version of me usually means butter; a curved one may not.
I'm made by folding butter into dough again and again for flaky layers.
A buttery crescent-shaped pastry, best with café au lait.

pearl: French bakers class it as a 'viennoiserie', which quietly admits where it came from.

title: Hands-on approach

clues.t: I taste things by touching them with my arms.
About two-thirds of my brain cells are in my arms.
I can squeeze through any gap bigger than my beak.
I squirt ink and change colour in a flash.
I have three hearts and blue blood.
Eight arms, lots of suckers, very clever.

pearl: Pedants say the plural is 'octopuses', since the word is Greek, not Latin. Even more pedants say 'octopodes'.

title: Sails that never leave port

clues.t: My design won an international competition in 1957.
I was budgeted at $7 million and ended up costing $102 million.
The first person to perform here sang to construction workers on their lunch break.
My roof shells were all cut from the geometry of a single sphere.
My white tiles came from Sweden, and Queen Elizabeth II opened me in 1973.
Shells (or sails) on Bennelong Point, beside a famous harbour bridge.

pearl: That first lunchtime singer was Paul Robeson in 1960. Bonus: it's World Heritage-listed, one of the youngest buildings ever to make the list.

title: Old soul

clues.t: One of my queens lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of my most famous tomb.
My most famous building was the tallest made by humans for about 3,800 years.
Most of my people live on a narrow strip of green in a huge desert.
My great river flows north.
Cats were sacred here, and some were mummified.
Pyramids, the Sphinx, the Nile and Cairo.

pearl: That queen was Cleopatra. History is longer than it looks.

title: Clear thinking

clues.t: A woman invented me in 1903 after watching a New York tram driver struggle in sleet.
Companies told her I had no commercial value.
My early versions were cranked by hand with a lever inside the vehicle.
A man who invented my intermittent setting sued Ford and Chrysler, and won.
His story became the film 'Flash of Genius'.
I swish back and forth across your car's front glass when it rains.

pearl: Mary Anderson's patent expired before cars took off, so she never earned a cent from it. Rude.

title: Play nice

clues.t: The carpet in one boy's house copies the carpet from The Shining.
One of my characters was the first toy ever advertised on TV.
A pizza delivery truck from me sneaks into many later films from my studio.
In 1995 I became the first feature film made entirely by computer.
A cowboy gets jealous of a new space ranger.
'To infinity and beyond!'

pearl: The TV-ad pioneer was Mr. Potato Head, back in 1952. Originally you supplied your own potato.

title: Backwards thinker
accept: leonardo di ser piero da vinci

clues.t: I often wrote my notes backwards, in mirror writing.
I reportedly bought caged birds at the market just to set them free.
My job application to a duke boasted about war machines and barely mentioned painting.
I sketched flying machines centuries before aeroplanes.
My most famous painting was stolen from the Louvre in 1911.
Renaissance genius behind the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper.

pearl: The Mona Lisa got way more famous after the theft. The best PR stunt nobody planned.

title: Nacho average snack

clues.t: I was invented in 1943 in a Mexican border town.
The cook wasn't around, so the maître d' improvised with what was in the kitchen.
My first customers were the wives of US soldiers stationed nearby.
I'm named after the man who invented me, by his nickname.
The original was simple: fried tortilla, cheese and jalapeño.
Corn chips smothered in melted cheese, salsa, guac and sour cream.

pearl: Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya made them in Piedras Negras. International Day of the Nacho is 21 October.

title: Hang in there

clues.t: Some of us have more neck bones than a giraffe.
Algae grows in my fur, giving me a greenish tinge.
Moths live in my fur too. Lovely.
I climb down from my tree roughly once a week just to go to the toilet.
Surprisingly, I'm a decent swimmer.
I spend life upside down in rainforest trees, moving very, very slowly.

pearl: Three-fingered sloths can have up to 10 neck vertebrae, letting them turn their heads a long way without moving their bodies. Efficient.

title: Off-balance budget

clues.t: I started going wrong when my builders reached the third floor.
I took nearly 200 years to finish, thanks partly to wars.
I'm a bell tower with seven bells.
Engineers spent about a decade nudging me back about 45 cm, finishing in 2001.
Legend says Galileo dropped balls off me to test gravity.
I'm a white marble tower in Italy that famously isn't straight.

pearl: Soft ground did it. The lean is now about 4 degrees, and tourists keep 'holding it up' for photos.

title: Samba seasoning

clues.t: I'm named after a tree.
I border every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
I have the largest Japanese community outside Japan.
A European empire was once ruled from my city, Rio de Janeiro.
I've won the men's football World Cup five times.
Carnival, the Amazon and Christ the Redeemer. Portuguese spoken.

pearl: The tree is brazilwood, prized for its red dye. The Portuguese royal court fled here from Napoleon in 1808.

title: Stair crazy

clues.t: When London's Harrods installed me in 1898, nervous customers were offered brandy at the top.
An early version of me was a ride at Coney Island in 1896.
My name was a trademark until a court ruled it had become an everyday word.
My name blends the Latin for ladder with 'elevator'.
Hong Kong has an outdoor system of me running about 800 m up a hill.
I'm a staircase that moves. Stand on the left, walk on the right? Or the other way round?

pearl: Otis lost the trademark in 1950. Brandy is no longer provided.

title: Somewhere over the box office

clues.t: The dog in me earned $125 a week, more than some human actors.
In the original book, the famous shoes were silver.
They were changed to red to show off a new colour process.
One pair of those shoes was stolen from a museum in 2005 and found by the FBI in 2018.
I open in sepia Kansas and burst into colour in a magical land.
Follow the yellow brick road. 'There's no place like home.'

pearl: Toto was played by a female Cairn terrier called Terry. She had more films than some of the cast.

title: Natural selection

clues.t: At university I joined a club that dined on unusual animals.
I nearly missed my big voyage because the captain didn't like the shape of my nose.
I once had a bassoon played to earthworms to see if they could hear.
I wrote a list of pros and cons before deciding to get married.
Finches and giant tortoises on the Galápagos Islands got me thinking.
I wrote 'On the Origin of Species' and gave the world evolution by natural selection.

pearl: The worms ignored the bassoon. Bonus: his final book was entirely about earthworms.

title: Love it or hate it (not that one)

clues.t: I'm made from leftover brewer's yeast.
A chemist created me in Melbourne in the early 1920s.
My name was picked out of a hat after a naming competition.
For a few years I was renamed 'Parwill', a dig at a British rival.
An Aussie company bought me back from American owners in 2017.
Black, salty, spread thinly on toast. A happy little Aussie spread.

pearl: 'Parwill' was a pun: if Marmite, then Parwill. It didn't work, and the old name came back.

title: River horse

clues.t: My closest living relatives are whales.
I ooze a red liquid that acts as sunscreen. It isn't blood or sweat.
Despite living in water, I can't really swim. I bounce along the bottom.
I spread my poo by spinning my tail like a fan.
My name is Greek for 'river horse'.
Huge mouth, tiny ears, wallowing in African rivers.

pearl: Hippos can open their jaws to about 150 degrees. The ultimate yawn.
